tasks.short: Design surveys about public transportation concerns

steps.what: Design transportation surveys around the population and public concerns to investigate

loop.purpose: Suggest question wording for the planner's selected research design
loop.input: Planner-defined objectives, population, sampling approach, constructs and response constraints
loop.output: Draft questions with objective mapping and unresolved design issues
loop.check: Planner checks leading wording, construct validity, accessibility, missing response options and whether questions can reveal unanticipated concerns
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; weak or unsupported questions are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native question libraries are tried first, but local wording needs contextual drafting

steps.what: Pilot and refine the transportation survey before approving the instrument

tasks.design: Use existing survey templates in {DOCS} before a bounded loop proposes question wording for the planner's research design. The planner checks validity and conducts the existing pilot before approving the instrument.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing clear questions takes effort after research objectives have been chosen.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can propose wording without deciding the population, sampling or constructs.
tasks.still_hard: Reaching underrepresented people and detecting concern categories the initial design misses.
tasks.human_edge: The planner judges whether responses will answer the real planning question.
tasks.altitude: A modest reduction in wording effort; research design and pilot interpretation remain human.

reach.task: Review question validity and sampling limitations

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound wording proposals may assist survey design, but no task-specific design-time saving is established by the digest's survey-response coding products.

assumptions: Boundary is instrument design and the existing pilot, excluding full survey fieldwork and response coding.

Within s1 the planner produces objectives, target population, sampling rationale, construct definitions, language/accessibility needs, response formats and excluded inferences before drafting. The 59.5 retained hours count design, capture and semantic correction; no free structured survey brief is assumed.

Pilot participants supply responses only after the draft is delivered during s2, before refinement. The pilot is unchanged baseline work, not newly transferred validation; no synthetic respondents replace it.

Test native survey templates first. Existing runtime earns no labour saving. Five extra focal hours cover template changes and failed-draft handling, and 3 other-role hours count survey-method specialist review of changed drafting conventions.
unknowns: Target population and existing pilot method
research_questions: Does question drafting save time after validity review and pilot-driven rewriting?

already_counted.description: Research design, brief capture and wording checks

incremental.description: Template changes and extra failed-draft handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact survey instrument, population, sampling design, response options and pilot-informed revisions checked in s2; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70*0.85+30=89.5; gross 10.5%, net 5.5% after 5 focal upkeep. Range covers failed drafts with no gain through 7 points of wording removed minus 5 upkeep. Research design and pilot work remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collaborate with professionals to develop sustainable transportation strategies

tasks.design: The planner discusses evidence and trade-offs with other professionals, using shared documents in {DOCS}. The collaboration remains the work rather than being replaced by generated strategy text.
tasks.previous_blocker: Strategy depends on competing objectives and agreement across organisations.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared records support access without establishing a saving in negotiation and joint reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling environmental, access, cost and delivery priorities.
tasks.human_edge: The planner understands context and builds agreement on workable choices.
tasks.altitude: Collaboration responsibility and decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate land-use and transport strategy choices
reach.learn: Land-use dependencies and public decision processes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: interdisciplinary strategy collaboration remains human; no clerical strategy-writing baseline is inferred.

assumptions: Boundary is professional collaboration, excluding separate evidence analysis and strategy publication.
Partners supply proposals during s1; the planner assesses them and develops joint choices there. No free structured agreed-strategy input is assumed.
Use native shared documents first; existing runtime earns no labour saving. Zero new upkeep because no automation or reporting demand is introduced.
unknowns: Strategy scale and partner decision rights
research_questions: Which disagreements require joint reasoning rather than further document preparation?

already_counted.description: Professional discussion and joint strategy development

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Substantive collaboration remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate transportation project needs and costs

steps.what: Evaluate project needs and verify transport quantities, cost sources and assumptions
Calculate project costs and compare explicit transportation project scenarios
Evaluate transportation needs and cost implications before recommending project priorities

tasks.design: Configure a checked calculation model in {SPREADSHEET} to reuse the planner's verified quantities, rates and scenario definitions. The planner retains the assessment of need, uncertain assumptions and the recommendation in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated scenario arithmetic can require manual copying between cost sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas and data links can repeat explicit calculations without ranking public needs automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether demand evidence and cost assumptions justify the project.
tasks.human_edge: The planner assesses impacts that a cost total cannot represent.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic with project judgement retained.

reach.task: Compare project effects with wider planning needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed scenario calculations can reuse verified costs and quantities; the proposed project-evaluation saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is project need and cost evaluation, excluding original engineering quantity production and final public investment decisions.

Existing engineers and cost-reference owners supply quantities and rates. In s1 the planner captures project scope, quantity/unit pairs, rate source and date, currency/base year, exclusions, contingency assumptions and scenario formulas; all verification and capture remains in 45%.

Missing quantities, stale rates or disputed scope return to manual evaluation. No free structured project-worthiness score is assumed. Three other-role hours count cost-reference owner mapping maintenance.
Test native spreadsheet formulas first; existing automatic arithmetic earns no new saving. Seven extra focal hours count assumption changes, calculation checks and unusual reconciliations.
unknowns: Current calculation automation and verified cost coverage
research_questions: Does scenario reuse save hands-on time after input checks and assumption changes?

already_counted.description: Needs assessment and structured cost-input capture

incremental.description: Assumption updates, model checks and extra reconciliation

approvals.approved_version: Exact project recommendation, quantity and rate versions, assumptions, scenarios and scope checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+30=75; gross 25%, net 18% after 7 focal upkeep. Range covers existing automated costing with zero new gain through 15 points of manual scenario work removed minus 7 upkeep. Need assessment and recommendation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define the traffic counting analysis and validate data coverage and exclusions
Aggregate traffic counting information and calculate specified comparisons
Analyze traffic counting patterns and explain limitations of the findings

tasks.design: Configure native transport-analysis software {OTHER} to repeat the planner's selected count aggregations and flag missing coverage. The planner checks results, interprets traffic patterns and states limitations in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated count aggregation can require manual spreadsheet preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native queries can calculate agreed intervals and comparisons once data definitions are verified.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting unusual counts and deciding whether coverage represents normal travel.
tasks.human_edge: The planner distinguishes a plausible table from a defensible planning conclusion.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated aggregation while analytical interpretation stays human.

reach.task: Assess whether traffic observations represent the intended population and period

evidence.claim: The digest identifies NDW as an open traffic-data source and PTV Visum as transport-analysis software; local data coverage and workflow savings are not established by these references.
Model knowledge: fixed traffic-count aggregation can be configured while coverage and interpretation remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is analysis of an existing counting program, excluding installing counters, field counts and independent transport modelling.

OTHER means transport-analysis software. Counting-program owners produce counts and metadata under the existing program. In s1 the planner captures source versions, site/direction IDs, timestamps and timezone, interval, vehicle classes, count units, coverage rules, exclusions and comparison formulas; all capture and validation remains in 25%.

Missing metadata or incompatible intervals go to manual reconciliation and s3 interpretation; no clean dataset or representative-period flag is assumed free. Four other-role hours count data-owner schema maintenance.
Test native aggregation first; already automatic processing earns no new labour saving. Eight extra focal hours count changed definitions, sample calculation checks and additional data exceptions.
unknowns: Count coverage and existing native aggregation
research_questions: Can native aggregation reproduce manually checked totals while exposing gaps and timezone changes?

already_counted.description: Analysis definition and structured data-contract checks

incremental.description: Definition changes, sample checks and extra data exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+35=60; gross 40%, net 32% after 8 focal upkeep. Range covers existing aggregation with zero new gain through 22 points of manual preparation removed minus 8 upkeep. Data validation and interpretation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The planner retains research and planning judgement while native calculations can reduce repeated data preparation.
reach: Coordinate survey validity, cost provenance and traffic coverage with specialist roles.
role.ambitious_version: More traceable transport evidence with all data preparation and judgement boundaries visible.
